profit.name: Profit
profit.title: Profit calculator
profit.intro: Type your sales and costs. Your profit shows as you type.
profit.metaDescription: Work out your shop's profit and profit % in seconds. Add stock, rent, salary and other costs. Free, no signup.
profit.empty: Type your sales to see your profit.
profit.shareProfit: My profit today: {amount} ({pct}). Calculate yours free: {link}
profit.shareProfitNoPct: My profit today: {amount}. Calculate yours free: {link}
profit.shareLoss: My result today: a loss of {amount}. Calculate yours free: {link}
profit.guideFormula: Profit = Sales − all costs. Profit % = Profit ÷ Sales × 100.
profit.guideExample: Sales Rs 25,000, stock Rs 15,000 and other costs Rs 1,500. Profit = 25,000 − 16,500 = Rs 8,500, which is 34% of sales.

faq.q: What is the difference between profit and sales?
faq.a: Sales is all the money that comes in. Profit is what is left after you pay every cost: stock, rent, salaries, electricity, transport and other costs.

faq.q: What is a good profit percentage for a small shop?
faq.a: It depends on what you sell. Shops that sell everyday items often have a lower %, and shops with special or handmade items a higher %. The best guide is your own number: check it every month and see if it goes up or down.

faq.q: Should I count goods my family takes from the shop?
faq.a: Yes. Goods taken for home use are a real cost, even when no money changes hands. Add them as a cost, so your profit on paper is not higher than the money in your pocket.

faq.q: Why does it show a loss?
faq.a: For the numbers you typed, your costs are higher than your sales. Check that every cost is correct, then look at the biggest cost first. The tip under the result tells you which one it is.

margin.name: Margin
margin.description: Profit per item, margin and markup.
margin.title: Margin calculator
margin.intro: Type what one item costs you and what you sell it for.
margin.metaTitle: Free profit margin and markup calculator
margin.metaDescription: Find the profit per item, margin % and markup % from cost and selling price. Free, no signup.
margin.quantityHint: How many items you sell. Leave empty for 1.
margin.marginVsMarkup: Margin is profit as a share of the selling price. Markup is profit as a share of the cost.
margin.totalProfit: Total profit for {quantity, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}
margin.totalLoss: Total loss for {quantity, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}
margin.empty: Type the cost and selling price to see your margin.
margin.shareProfit: Cost {cost}, price {price}: profit {amount} per item ({margin} margin). Calculate yours free: {link}
margin.shareLoss: Cost {cost}, price {price}: loss {amount} per item. Calculate yours free: {link}
margin.guideTitle: How to calculate margin and markup
margin.guideFormula: Profit per item = Price − Cost. Margin % = Profit ÷ Price × 100. Markup % = Profit ÷ Cost × 100.
margin.guideExample: Cost Rs 85, price Rs 110, 100 items. Profit per item Rs 25, margin 22.7%, markup 29.4%, total profit Rs 2,500.

faq.q: What is the difference between margin and markup?
faq.a: Margin is the profit divided by the selling price. Markup is the profit divided by the cost. For the same item, the markup % is always higher than the margin %.

faq.q: How do I calculate the margin of one item?
faq.a: Take the cost away from the selling price to get the profit per item. Then divide it by the selling price and multiply by 100. Example: (110 − 85) ÷ 110 × 100 = 22.7%.

faq.q: Why can't the margin be 100% or more?
faq.a: A 100% margin would mean the item cost you nothing. As long as an item costs something, the margin stays below 100%. Markup has no such limit.
It multiplies the profit per item, so you can see the total profit for a batch, for example 100 bars of soap.

price.name: Selling price
price.description: The right price for the profit you want.
price.title: Selling price calculator
price.intro: Find the price that gives you the profit you want.
price.metaDescription: Find the right selling price from your cost and the markup or margin you want. Free, no signup.
price.modeMarkupHelp: Markup: the % is added on top of the cost.
price.modeMarginHelp: Margin: the % is the part of the selling price that is profit.
price.empty: Type the cost and the profit % you want.
price.marginTooHigh: Margin must be less than 100%. To double the cost, choose Markup and type 100%.
price.shareMarkup: Cost {cost} + {pct} markup: sell for {price}. Calculate yours free: {link}
price.shareMargin: Cost {cost} with a {pct} margin: sell for {price}. Calculate yours free: {link}
price.guideTitle: How to find the selling price
price.guideFormula: Markup: Price = Cost × (1 + % ÷ 100). Margin: Price = Cost ÷ (1 − % ÷ 100).
price.guideExample: Cost Rs 85 with 20%: markup gives Rs 102.00 and margin gives Rs 106.25. Rounded up to the next Rs 10, the markup price is Rs 110.

faq.q: Should I use markup or margin?
faq.a: Use markup if you think "add 20% to my cost". Use margin if you think "20% of the price should be profit". For the same %, margin gives a higher price.
Round prices like Rs 105 or Rs 110 are easier for customers and for giving change. Rounding up never lowers your profit.

faq.q: How do I choose the profit %?
faq.a: Look at what similar shops charge, then check the result with the margin calculator. Remember that this % must also pay your rent, salaries and other fixed costs.

faq.q: Can I use it for services?
faq.a: Yes. Put the cost of your materials and your time as the cost, then choose the profit you want.

breakEven.name: Break-even
breakEven.description: Sales you need to cover your costs.
breakEven.title: Break-even calculator
breakEven.intro: See how much you must sell to cover your monthly costs.
breakEven.metaDescription: Find the sales you need each month and each day to cover your fixed costs. Free, no signup.
breakEven.fixedHint: Rent, salaries, electricity and other costs you pay even when you sell nothing.
breakEven.marginHint: Not sure? Work it out with the <link>margin calculator</link>.
breakEven.marginInvalid: Margin must be more than 0% and not more than 100%.
breakEven.perDay: Sales needed per day ({days, plural, one {# open day} other {# open days}})
breakEven.explain: Sell more than this and you make a profit. Sell less and you make a loss.
breakEven.empty: Type your fixed costs and your average margin.
breakEven.share: To cover {fixed} of fixed costs at a {margin} margin, I need sales of {monthly} a month ({daily} a day). Calculate yours free: {link}
breakEven.guideTitle: How to calculate your break-even point
breakEven.guideFormula: Sales needed per month = Fixed costs ÷ (Margin % ÷ 100). Per day = Monthly sales ÷ open days.
breakEven.guideExample: Fixed costs Rs 60,000 and a 20% margin: 60,000 ÷ 0.20 = Rs 300,000 a month. With 26 open days, that is about Rs 11,538 a day.

faq.a: It is the amount you must sell to pay all your fixed costs. Sell more and you make a profit; sell less and you make a loss.
Costs you pay every month even if you sell nothing: rent, salaries, electricity, loan payments, internet and similar costs. Stock you buy to sell is not a fixed cost.

faq.q: Where do I find my average margin?
faq.a: Use the margin calculator for your main products and take a typical value. If you sell many different items, divide your monthly profit before fixed costs by your monthly sales.

faq.q: Why does a higher margin lower the break-even point?
faq.a: Each sale leaves more money to pay the fixed costs, so you need fewer sales to cover them.
